messages:
maria: Deploybot flagged retag drift on eu-ecr for image redwood/runner:v2.3.1 — provenance metadata changed during mirror. Holding promotion. Logs: `deploybot: provenance mismatch digest=sha256:abc123 expected=sha256:def456`. Can we decide rollback vs retag?
deploybot: Auto-action: push quarantined. Canary traffic paused. Suggested action: `pin-to-digest sha256:def456` or allow manual retag. Reaction :rotating_light:
devin: ack. I'm seeing the builder's post-process updated `org.redwood.build.metadata.build_id` when cache hit occurred. Likely a parallel publish race. Does the commit's CI artifact match digest def456?
samir: quick check: release notes already published? If we roll back we'll need to update release notes and call out the canary delay.
caroline: FYI our EU change window closes in 2h. If we don't resolve before then, ops wants to freeze and schedule manual promote tomorrow.
maria: Release notes were uploaded — tag v2.3.1 -> def456. If we pin to previous digest (abc123) we'd need a hotfix release to keep artifacts consistent.
devin: I can retag builder to force digest def456 -> new digest via republish, but that re-signs attestation and will change provenance. Safer option: pin callers to abc123 and rollback canary.
samir: Vote: rollback canary to abc123 and mark v2.3.1 hotfix to follow. +1 from me.
maria: +1 from me. Also file a follow-up: check deploybot mirror idempotency to avoid parallel publish race.
release-bot: Policy check: For provenance mismatch, automated fallback is `pin-to-previous-digest` when canary_throughput < 50 TPS. Canary is 12 TPS -> allowed. Will execute rollback in 30s unless someone objects.
caroline: no objection from infra side. Proceed.
deploybot: Executing rollback: pinned route `canary` -> sha256:abc123. Canary resumed. Notifying monitoring and creating ticket `RB-1134`.
maria: Thanks. After stabilization let's schedule a backfill to republish signed attestation under controlled single-publisher window tomorrow 09:00 UTC.
